title: Sliding Subarray Beauty
summary: Given an integer array, determine the beauty of each subarray of size k by identifying the x-th smallest negative integer or 0 if fewer than x negative integers are present.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the beauty of each subarray of size k by identifying the x-th smallest negative integer or 0 if fewer than x negative integers are present. Return an array of n - k + 1 integers representing the beauty of each subarray in order.
constraints: For each contiguous window of length k, sort only its negative values conceptually.
Its beauty is the xth smallest negative value, or zero when fewer than x negatives exist.
Return the beauty of every window from left to right.
hints: Values lie in the small fixed range -50 through 50, so maintain a frequency array.
Initialize counts for the first length-k window.
Scan negative values in ascending order until cumulative frequency reaches x; slide by removing the outgoing value and adding the incoming value.
The frequency scan exactly simulates sorted negative order, and each update preserves counts for the current window.
editorial: The frequency scan exactly simulates sorted negative order, and each update preserves counts for the current window.

tests.explanation: The successive second-smallest negative values are -1, -2, and -2.
Each two-value window contains two negatives, so its larger negative is returned.
